images.title: Heads Down in the Shallows
images.story: A flock of flamingos paced the shallow pool, dipping their curved beaks underwater in sync like synchronized swimmers ignoring the crowd. One turned completely upside down to sift through the green sediment while another preened along the damp stone edge. The morning light barely cut through the leafy canopy, leaving the water quiet and dark.

images.title: Silver Fur on Weathered Stucco
images.story: This silver langur sat perched on the rusted wire, watching visitors with complete indifference. Years of tropical humidity had streaked the white wall behind him into patches of dark moss and fine cracks. He stayed motionless long enough for me to frame his grizzled coat against the weathered green bars.

images.title: Golden Infant in Mom's Grip
images.story: Silver langur babies are born a bright apricot orange, making this little one stand out dramatically against his mother's charcoal coat. She anchored herself to the cage bars with one arm while tucking him securely to her chest. Despite the rust and peeling paint around them, her grip was gentle and sure.

images.title: Wide Grip on Iron Bars
images.story: A young langur stretched both arms across the vertical bars, looking straight down the barrel of my lens. His pinkish chest and fluffy gray crest caught the shaded morning light filtering into the enclosure. He held that wide stance just long enough to see if I was carrying anything edible.

images.title: Reaching for Fresh Leaves
images.story: Gaining some confidence, the golden baby scrambled up the green railing to snatch at the leaves his mother was chewing. She leaned calmly against the corner pillar, letting him paw at her face without batting an eye. It was amusing to watch him try his best to mimic adult breakfast habits.

images.title: White Swan on Still Water
images.story: A lone white swan drifted silently along the green moat, barely leaving a wake behind its tail. Just past the tall perimeter fence, the distant hum of morning traffic on Nguyen Binh Khiem kept rolling by. Framed by dark leaves in the foreground, the bird floated on like none of that rush mattered.

images.title: Coral Beneath White Feathers
images.story: A flamingo curled its slender neck back, flashing the bright coral plumage tucked beneath its wings. It seemed indifferent to the afternoon chatter around the pool, methodically grooming each quill. The muted enclosure light caught the pale yellow ring of its eye.

images.title: Loops and Pale Feathers
images.story: Its neck curved into an improbable loop while its bill worked along the back of its wing. Shaded by the trees, the white feathers took on cool grey tones against the soft background. It paused for just a second, eye locked straight into my lens.

images.title: Ripples and Pink Stilts
images.story: One flamingo bowed low over the dark pool, sifting water while droplets rolled off the tip of its black beak. Long pink stilt legs carried it through the shallows with slow, measured strides. In the background, another bird mirrored its quiet rhythm.

images.title: Cobalt Neck in the Shade
images.story: The peacock stood upright on the lawn, showing off an electric cobalt neck against the green gloom of the tree canopy. Its delicate crest stayed rigid, like tiny antennas tuned to every footstep on the path. It gave me a sideways glance before strutting deeper into the shadows.

images.title: Double-Decker on the Dirt
images.story: Two giant tortoises formed an unexpected two-tier stack right in the middle of the dusty enclosure. The one underneath stared ahead with patient resignation, entirely committed to waiting things out. Watching them move was a masterclass in slow-motion persistence.

images.title: Whiskers by the Pool Rim
images.story: A lone otter rested its front paws on the concrete ledge, wet coat glistening under the filtered afternoon light. Its whiskers twitched at the surface ripples before it decided I was harmless. A second later, it slipped back into the cool water without a splash.
